name: R Draconis
blurb: A pulsating red giant that brightens and fades every 246 days; SPHEREx caught it bright in August 2026 and faint in September 2025.
known_type_ref: AAVSO VSX via VizieR B/vsx/vsx (OID 13673), fetched 2026-11-14
discovery_ref: Brief target; discovery reference not looked up.
notes: Period 246.12 d, maximum JD 2457370.0, V 6.7-13.2 (VSX; the brief quotes 245.6 d). Saturates every SPHEREx detector, so brightness is measured only as a relative quantity from the unsaturated PSF wings (9-13 px ring). Checked 2026-11-15 (probes/variables/verify.py, verify_followup.py): across 399 exposures (Apr 2025-Sep 2026) a sine fit at the VSX period gives peak-to-peak 1.33 mag (1.01-1.44, 68% over resampled passes) at 0.75-1.1 um and 0.70 mag (0.66-0.85) at 4.4-5.0 um, maxima 0.02 and 0.04 cycles after the VSX prediction. Two comparison stars of similar brightness measured the same way swing at most 7% as much. 1.65-2.4 um fails (a comparison star swings 0.43 times as much) and 2.4-3.8 um fails (rests on one pass); neither is published. The data alone give a best period of 253 d but only 144-276 d (68%), so the period is the catalogue's. NEOWISE per-visit medians (2014-2024, saturated) follow the same ephemeris with 0.33 mag W1 semi-amplitude. Relative only: no calibrated flux. Published in web/data/variability.json (probes/variables/export_web.py).
sources: https://irsa.ipac.caltech.edu/SIA (spherex_dr1, spherex_qr3, spherex_dr1_deep, spherex_qr3_deep; 2,493 frames, fetched 2026-11-14)
photometry_source: AllWISE J163240.19+664517.9 (saturated; values are not reliable magnitudes)
